overview: Two opposite evolutionary patterns — one describes related species growing apart in form, the other describes unrelated species growing similar in form.
genZNote: Divergent: same starting line, different finish lines. Convergent: different starting lines, somehow the same finish line.

aspects.label: Pattern
aspects.valueA: Related species accumulate differences over time, becoming increasingly distinct.
aspects.valueB: Unrelated species independently evolve similar traits due to similar environmental pressures.

aspects.label: Ancestry
aspects.valueA: Species share a recent common ancestor.
aspects.valueB: Species do not share a recent common ancestor.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Darwin's finches evolving different beak shapes from a common ancestor.
aspects.valueB: Dolphins (mammals) and sharks (fish) both evolving streamlined, fin-shaped bodies.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Darwin's finches on the Galapagos Islands are the classic textbook example of divergent evolution driven by different food sources.
overlay.memoryTrick: Divergent = diverging apart from one ancestor. Convergent = converging toward a similar form from different ancestors.
overlay.commonMisconception: Convergent evolution does not mean the species are related — it specifically highlights that similar traits can evolve completely independently.
